description.value: Duncanby Lodge is a remote, all-inclusive salmon and halibut fishing destination in Rivers Inlet on BC's breathtaking Central Coast, family-owned by the Keay family since 2003. Guests arrive by chartered floatplane from Vancouver and can choose between self-guided and guided fishing in a fleet ranging from 18.5-foot centre consoles to 23–26-foot Grady Whites. The surrounding wilderness offers wildlife encounters with humpback whales, bears, and eagles across 40 kilometres of ocean and mountain scenery.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms Duncanby Lodge is a real, actively operating all-inclusive salmon and halibut fishing lodge in Rivers Inlet, BC, with bookings open for 2026. Access is exclusively by chartered floatplane from Vancouver's Seair Seaplanes terminal; no road access is mentioned or implied. No cycling-related amenities, bike storage, or cyclist-oriented services appear anywhere on the website, and the travel information focuses entirely on floatplane logistics and luggage limits.
concerns: Lodge is accessible only by chartered floatplane from Vancouver (Seair Seaplanes); no road access exists, making it effectively unreachable by bicycle — relevance to cycling tourism directory is very low.

Physical lodge location is in Rivers Inlet (GPS per website: 51°24'16.63"N 127°38'43.69"W); mailing address listed on website is 9076 River Rd, Delta, BC V4G 1B5 — these are different locations; OSM coordinates appear to reflect the physical lodge site.
No cycling-related amenities, bike infrastructure, or cyclist-oriented services mentioned anywhere on the website.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operational commercial lodge with active 2026 season bookings. Floatplane-only access means cyclists cannot arrive by bike, but this does not meet any of the enumerated exclusion criteria.
